SK2017 The exception names a parameter that does not exist

An ArgumentException-family constructor is handed a paramName string literal that names no parameter in scope, and exactly one parameter in scope is one edit away from it.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since1.3
ReSharperSuspiciousParameterNameInArgumentNullException (resharper_suspicious_parameter_name_in_argument_null_exception_highlighting)

Why

paramName is an ordinary string, so throw new ArgumentNullException("vlaue") compiles and ships. What it produces at runtime is a message, an ArgumentException.ParamName and a log line all naming a parameter the method does not have, which sends the reader of the failure to the wrong argument. The same slip is easier still on the rest of the family, where paramName is positional and sits next to the message. nameof is the repair: it is the same string, checked by the compiler, and it cannot go stale under a rename.

Example

Instead of:

void Write(string value) {
    if (value is null) {
        throw new ArgumentNullException("vlaue");
    }
}

Write:

void Write(string value) {
    if (value is null) {
        throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(value));
    }
}

When it does not fire

The argument is located by the constructor symbol's parameter named paramName, never by position, so the overloads where the same slot is a message — ArgumentException(message, innerException), ArgumentNullException(message, innerException) — are not touched, and a named argument is followed to the right slot. Only a plain string literal is examined: nameof, a constant, an interpolation, a variable and an empty literal are all left alone. ⚠ The names in scope are every parameter the C# scoping rules put there, which is deliberately more than the enclosing method: a lambda's and a local function's own parameters, an indexer's parameters, the implicit value of a set, init, add and remove accessor, the containing type's primary-constructor parameters, and the parameters of every enclosing function — so a nested local function that validates its caller's argument by name is correct and is not reported. The walk stops at a static lambda or static local function, whose enclosing parameters it may not name, and at the containing type, whose outer type's primary constructor is not in scope. ⚠ A literal that resembles nothing in scope is a deliberate false negative. The rule reports only where exactly one parameter in scope is a case-only difference or a single edit — insertion, deletion, substitution or adjacent transposition — away from the literal, and both names are at least three characters long. Where two parameters are equally close, or none is, the rule cannot say which name was meant; reporting there would be a finding whose repair skala fix could not write, and doc 08 ships this rule with a safe fix. A paramName copied from a different overload, or left behind by a rename to an unrelated word, is therefore silent rather than guessed at.
